summary: High-stayed videos use a 'Counter-Intuitive Truth' hook that immediately challenges a common assumption (e.g., cars crushing is good).
High-stayed titles pose a direct question that creates a curiosity gap about the safety or capability of the viewer.
Avoid academic, observational, or 'Why/How' style hooks (e.g., 'Why some foods...'), which have lower retention compared to direct, personal-stakes narrative hooks.
The data shows a massive drop-off for 'household objects' or 'science discovery' topics; pivot toward high-stakes, relatable, or survival-based scenarios.
Maintain high-stayed performance by front-loading the 'reveal' of the concept within the first 3 seconds, rather than building up to it.
winning_hooks: जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है।
सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars एक के ऊपर एक रख दी जाएं।
Movies में T. rex गाड़ी का पीछा करता है। पर असली T. rex शायद दौड़ ही नहीं सकता था।
avoid: Starting with observational titles like 'Why Your Smoke Detector Is Radioactive'.
Over-explaining scientific phenomena in the first 5 seconds without a 'What if' or 'Imagine' scenario.
Using technical titles that feel like an educational lecture rather than a personal experience.
next_experiment: A/B test the same topic using a 'Survival/What-if' hook (e.g., 'What if you were in X scenario?') vs. a 'Fact-based' hook (e.g., 'The truth about X') to isolate if the 'you' focus is the primary driver of the 60%+ stayed_pct.
